newsitem.title: JAPAN: Major Japanese retailers' sales drop in May.
newsitem.headline: Major Japanese retailers' sales drop in May.

text.p: Japan's big retailers said Tuesday that their sales dropped about 5 percent last month, adding they did not expect a sharp recovery soon.
An increase in the national sales tax continued to hurt consumption, which had already been undermined by the nation's weak economic recovery, industry analysts said.

Supermarket sales declined 4.6 percent from the previous year to 1.34 trillion yen ($11.7 billion) in May, while department store sales slipped 5.1 percent to 658.9 billion yen ($5.77 billion), industry groups said on Tuesday.
"Sales are not strong and we cannot expect a dramatic boost towards the end of the year," an analyst at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics said.

The department stores association said sales of large and expensive items were slow in particular, as demand waned after rises in advance of an April 1 increase in the consumption tax rate to 5 percent from 3 percent.
The negative impact of the tax increase on individual customers was smaller in May than in April but purchases by corporate customers remained sluggish, it added.
Many large retailers said that unusually low temperatures for May affected sales of clothing, which accounts for a large portion of sales to individual customers.

Major department store operator Isetan Co. Ltd was one of few operators that enjoyed brisk sales of summer clothing in May. A spokesman said purchases by individual customers almost returned to the level before the tax increase.
Large retailers said they were not sure when their sales would start to gain speed.
The Isetan spokesman said the retailer may need some more time until overall sales, including sales to corporate customers, recover to last year's level.

"(Japanese) companies' profits are rising, but that has not benefited us yet," the Mitsukoshi spokesman said. Many Japanese companies have been able to boost their profits, due to radical cost-cutting steps and the weak yen.
